content: The test image shows a young soybean plant collapsed at soil level with a rotted/wilted stem and dead brown leaves — classic damping-off or root/stem rot pattern. Top candidates: Pythium_damping_off, Rhizoctonia, Phytophthora.

- Hand holding the collapsed plant — showing field-level scouting of a dead plant

- **Pythium_damping_off**: Reference shows pre-emergence/very early cotyledon stage only, much younger than test ✗
- **Fusarium/Charcoal_Rot/Brown_Stem_Rot**: Affect more mature plants with internal discoloration, not early seedling collapse ✗
- **Sudden_death_syndrome**: Characteristic interveinal chlorosis on leaves — absent here ✗

The complete post-emergence collapse of a young plant with stem rot at the soil line, in sandy soil, most closely matches **Phytophthora** root and stem rot.
